rationale: This is a kitchen-sink merge of the two best archive signals' existing legs (ppegt growth / capx-dp expansion crossed with oancf-capx / cash-ROA funding) with no new economic content, so it is a cosmetic averaging variant whose most likely outcome is an alpha somewhere between the two parents and a mechanism that becomes harder, not easier, to attribute.

The diagnosis (null FMB slope plus strong tail alpha implies an outlier-dominated product) is correct and the operator swap is cleanly attributable, but replacing MUL with SUMRANK converts a conditional interaction into an additive blend of an investment measure and a liquidity measure, so a failure will be uninformative about whether the original conditioning or merely the scaling was responsible.

target_name: Capex intensity with weak debt-service capacity
rationale: FFO-to-debt is a genuinely distinct fragility channel from the cash-flow-gap, cash-buffer, and working-capital legs already tested and the sign logic is internally consistent, but the ratio's denominator (dltt+dlc) approaches zero for low-leverage firms, so the claimed high coverage and the stability of the industry z-score leg are both doubtful and 1% winsorization may not tame it.

Investment intensity interacted with earnings/profit uncertainty is well-trodden published territory (asset-growth and investment anomalies concentrating in high-uncertainty, high-idiosyncratic-volatility, limits-to-arbitrage subsamples), and the proposal itself concedes this is a repackaging of a previously flagged gen-0 idea rather than a new mechanism.

target_name: Capex into a multi-year gross-profitability decline
rationale: The diagnosis of the archive's capital-productivity signal (strong slope, negligible alpha from a noisy one-year turnover change) motivates a substantive horizon-and-measure change to a five-year gross-profitability trend that shifts the concept from utilization wobble to structural erosion, with a consistent sign and an attributable single-element edit, though the five-year window will cost coverage.

This is structurally identical to the archive's gen-1 "Financing-deficit-weighted capacity growth" with ib+dp substituted for oancf — a proxy-swap robustness check rather than a new signal — and since every archive signal sits in the 0.07–0.13 coverage band regardless of whether oancf is used, the central justification of materially higher coverage is unlikely to hold.
